Petrus quoque Loth vitam approbat, dicens: Et justum Loth oppressum a nefandorum injuria ac luxuriosa conversatione eripuit; aspectu enim et auditu justus erat: habitans apud eos, qui de die in diem animam justi iniquis operibus cruciabant (II Petr. II). Hinc Joannes Pergami Ecclesiae scribit, dicens: Scio ubi habitas, ubi sedes est Satanae, et habes nomen meum, et non negasti fidem meam (Apoc. II); Paulus quoque 1095Cdiscipulos laudat et roborat, dicens: In medio nationis pravae et perversae inter quos lucetis quasi luminaria in mundo. Verbum vitae continentes (Philip. II).

Istis auctoritatibus satis constat, quantae sit virtutis pravos hominum mores tolerare, quando ex majori reproborum malitia majora electis crescunt meritorum lucra quia scriptum est: Quanto plus Pharao populum Dei premebat, tanto plus multiplicabatur (Exod. I).

Quae autem sint filiae, inter quas Ecclesia sive sancta anima sicut lilium inter spinas commorari dicitur, ex ipsa comparatione colligitur quia quae spinis comparantur, constat 87 quod in adversam partem recipiantur, quae ideo filiae nuncupantur, quia 1095Dex semine nequam perversae doctrinae, sive ex mala animi conceptione generantur. At Ecclesia sive quaevis fidelis anima, quae Christi per fidem et operationem est sponsa, ut lilium inter spinas esse possit, se regenti et protegenti, gratiosa laude per aliam comparationem occurrit, dicens: Sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, etc.

VERS. 3.-- Sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, sic dilectus meus inter filios. Sub umbra illius quem desideraveram sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.

Dilectus, inquit, meus comparavit me lilio inter spinas, virtutem suam servanti, quod quamvis mihi suo munere concesserit, tamen ut hoc fierem proprio me exemplo docuit. Quia sicut malus arbor fructifera tria in se habens utilia quibus reficit, 1096Ahoc esse fructum, odorem et umbram; inter ligna silvarum quoque, quae utique infructuosa sunt, incomparabilis habetur, ita dilectus meus fructu et odore sanctitatis, et justitiae, et doctrinae, atque umbra protectionis suae, quibus in se credentes reficit, docet et defendit; inter filios, id est Judaeos exstitit, qui primo quidem filii fuerunt et nunc esse volunt, sed non sunt quia de eis Deus dixit: Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me (Isa. I); et alibi: Filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi, filii alieni inveterati sunt et claudicaverunt a semitis suis (Psal. XVII): qui jactant se filios esse Abrahae, sed non sunt quia opera non habent (Joan. VIII), et ideo sunt ligna infructuosa et inutilia, atque ob hoc succidenda et in ignem mittenda. Nam inter talia 1096Bligna aeterno incendio capta in arbore crucis pependit, de qua dulcissimum sui corporis et sanguinis fructum mihi profudit, quo sibi credentes quotidie reficit: ipsi autem quasi ligna silvestria, non solum nullum boni operis protulerunt fructum, sed etiam amarissimum suae malitiae et impietatis profuderunt succum, clamantes: Crucifige, crucifige (Joan. XIX.), et: Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros (Matth. XVII).

Sub hujus ergo arboris umbra, hoc est Novi Testamenti refrigerio et defensione consolatoria quam desiderabam multo jam tempore, in antiquis patribus, magno desiderio tempora lenientis et refrigerantis gratiae suspirantibus, jam tandem post Christi adventum, passionem, resurrectionem et ascensionem 1096Csedi fide inconcussa et stabili. Lex enim aestu quodam inclementiae et incurabilis poenae, quando dicebat: Si quis haec vel illa fecerit, morte moriatur (Exod. XIX), me diu affecerat; gratia vero talem aestum umbra misericordiae et remedio poenitentiae movit, sub qua umbra desiderabili non ambulavi, non steti, sed potius sedi et requievi, quia 88 hoc pietatis decretum ipsius Domini mei auctoritate confirmatum immutabiliter tenendum suscepi.

Haec nimirum arbor lignum est vitae, cujus umbra et protectio divina quam fundant rami illius, rami honoris et gratiae, qui videlicet sunt diversarum oppositiones virtutum contra mundanarum fervores tentationum: utpote contra superbiam, 1096Dnecessaria est humilitatis oppositio; contra iram, patientiae; contra luxuriam, castitatis et continentiae; contra contumaciam, obedientiae; contra avaritiam, largitatis et misericordiae; contra lites et contentiones, pacis et concordiae; contra invidiam et odium, dilectionis, utque breviter comprehendamus, contra omnes certe mundi hujus oblectationes et tentationes opponenda est recordatio futurae miseriae malorum et gloriae justorum.

Talium nempe umbrarum effusiones protegunt animam ab aestu carnalium suggestionum et delectationum, sub quibus, quia desiderabam, sedi, hoc est requievi, quoniam quidem gratum et salubre in eis protegentis gratiae refrigerium inveni.

Et fructus ejus, haud dubium quin illius mali id 1097Aest Christi, sponsi et Domini mei, dulcis gutturi meo, quia utilitas et suavitas praeceptorum ejus, dulcis et placens est palato cordis mei, et capacitati mentis meae. Sive fructus hujus mali pendentis in arbore crucis dulcis est gutturi meo, quia corporis et sanguinis Christi perceptio dulcedinem, et sanitatem infundit pectori meo, et ipsa plane est perfecta corporis et ani mae meae refectio.

Aliter quoque filii inter quos dicitur sponsus commorari, sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, accipiuntur electi qui filii Dei nuncupative dicuntur propter observantiam mandatorum ejus pro quibus aeternae vitae haereditatem ab ipso Patre suo coelesti consequentur, inter quos Christus velut malus inter ligna silvarum moratur, quia sicut malus 1097Bomnia ligna silvarum pulchritudine et fructuum odore et suavitate praecellit, ita Christus omnes sanctos virtutum decore, et doctrinae dulcedine antecedit, sicut de ipso scriptum est: Speciosus forma prae filiis hominum, diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis; propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus oleo exsultationis prae participibus tuis (Psal. XLIV).

Sub cujus umbra seu Ecclesia, quia sive sacramentorum, sive mandatorum, sive donorum, illius rami per totam mundi latitudinem diffusis, mirabiliter protegitur et consolatur ab omni aestu tristitiae et perturbationis, secura et immobilis permanens, per spem futurae retributionis, cujus fructus dulcis est gutturi ejus, quia omnia eloquiorum ejus mystica, sacramentorumque venerabilia instituta, quae 1097Cex occulta divinitatis suae protulit sapientia, dulcia et grata sunt menti ea devote complectenti et veneranti, 89 propter eam quae inde ei confertur salutem, sine fine vegetantem et reficientem.

Quem vero effectum hujus fructus dulcedo et suavitas habeat, quid sublimius et perfectius pariat subdendo manifestat.

VERS. 4.-- Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam, ordinavit in me charitatem.

Effectus introductionis hujus processit ex causa bene placentis et ideo magno mentis studio suscepti fructus, quia quo plus Dei praecepta appetuntur, tanto amplius ad majora semper appetenda, amore divino intromittuntur. Fructum quidem 1097Dillum qui profluxit, et adhuc profluit de illa gloriosa et excellentissima arbore Domino Jesu Christo non omnes aequaliter accipiunt: quia alius istum, alius illum, juxta quod sapit et diligit accipit.

Isti enim magis sapit et placet virtus patientiae, illi obedientiae; isti humilitatis, illi continentiae; istum magis oblectat sedulitas orationis, illum lectionis, jejuniorum; et in toto virtutum gratiarum divino munere comparant species.

Est autem quoddam quasi singulare et quasi seorsum in quodam secreto consistens repositorium, quod cella nuncupatur, prae sui quadam angustia, eo quod paucos in suos admittat recessus, ubi est illius fructus dulcedo et suavitas recondita quae laetificat cor hominis (Psal. CIII), et omnem vitiorum excoquit humorem, 1098Aevangelicum videlicet praeceptum de charitatis utilitate. Quod vini nomine recte appellatur, quia sicut vinum se purgando, omnem a se rejicit pestiferum et suo naturali colore omnem noxium excoquit humorem; ita charitatis praeceptum, omnem a corde vitiorum fugat pestem, et omnes animi expellit passiones, quia nemo potest et charitatem habere et malus esse; atque ideo hujus plena intelligentia merito nuncupatur cella vinaria.

Illi ergo qui sub illius salutiferae arboris ramis delectantur requiescere et dulcissimum sanctitatis fructum sine fastidio colligere, ad hanc quandoque perfectionem pervenient, ut sine obstaculo cellam vinariam intrent, quia non est eis haec via angusta, quibus occlusa funditus est mundanae voluptatis 1098Bvia, lata et spatiosa. Angusta enim est hujus praecepti via, quia difficilis videtur multis et laboriosa cum dicitur: Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his qui oderunt vos (Matth. V).

Sed quia a multis sanctis legimus observatum, non est difficile hoc praeceptum nisi his, qui nondum perfecto gustaverunt dulcedinem fructuum, id est mandatorum divinorum. Haec est ergo cella vinaria perfectio, et angustam viam libere intrantibus, suaviter sapiens et ob hoc perfectibilis divini praecepti intelligentiae de charitatis excellentia.

Verum quia ipsa charitas in diversa respicit, necessarius est in ea 90 ordo attendendus ut scire possit quo loco sit ponendus quivis affectus et quis prior, quis posterior accipiendus. Unde cum praemisisset: 1098CIntroduxit me rex in cellam vinariam, subdit, et ordinavit in me charitatem. Iste enim est ordo sanctae dilectionis, ut primo Deum, deinde proximum, postremo et ipsum inimicum diligamus. Necessarius nempe est ordo iste, quia impossibile est ut quis diligat proximum, vel, quod difficilius est, inimicum, nisi diligat Deum, dum istorum dilectionis causa sit dilectio Dei, fiatque hoc modo possibile quod fuit impossibile. Quod enim necesse est esse, impossibile est non esse, et quod necesse est non esse impossibile est esse. Est autem necesse esse amorem Dei ubi est amor proximi, quia nemo diligit proximum propter Deum, nisi diligat Deum: necesse est autem non esse amorem Dei, ubi non 1098Dest amor proximi, juxta Joannis vocem quia: Qui non diligit fratrem suum quem vidit, Deum quem non videt, quomodo potest diligere? (I Joan. IV.) Non vero semper necesse est non esse amorem Dei, ubi non est amor inimici, quia potest contingere ut diligens Deum, non habeat inimicum quem diligat propter Deum: si autem habet, tunc necesse est non esse amorem Dei, ubi non est amor inimici quia probat se non diligere Deum qui non vult diligere inimicum propter Deum.

Videtur ergo ordo iste, ut dictum est, esse necessarius, quando decernitur impossibilem esse dilectionem proximi nisi praecedat dilectio Dei, secundum illum tamen amorem qui est secundum Deum, non qui secundum saeculum. Amor quippe 1099Asaeculi est absque amore Dei quia ille secundum carnem, iste secundum spiritum.

Est autem duplex modus dilectionis secundum carnem; unus qui omnino contra Deum est, sicut est malorum pro iniquitatis communione invicem se diligentium; alter vero qui non est contra Deum sicut est parentum cognatorum, et amicorum, cui tamen amori praeponendus est semper amor Dei, et propter Deum amor cujusque proximi. Sed primus modus secundum carnem omnino a praesenti alienus est loco, quia inordinatus est totus Deoque contrarius; alter vero qui non est contra Deum, a praesenti non abhorret loco, si tamen sit ordinatus, quia si plus in Deo diligitur homo quam Deus, tunc est inordinatus.

1099BPotest autem non absurde accipi, ut dicamus geminum esse ordinem charitatis, unum in Deo, alterum in proximo: scriptum est enim: Deus charitas est (I Joan. IV): in hac autem charitate quae Deus est, ordinem debet discere, scire et intelligere Ecclesia, sive quaelibet sancta anima ut primo loco dicat Patrem quasi vocem, secundo Filium quasi ex voce verbum, tertio Spiritum sanctum quasi ex voce et verbo procedentem rationem. Non autem eo sensu dicat, quasi aliquis sit gradus in Trinitate, 91 quod impium est dicere, sed ut charitatem illam, id est Deum, quem debet diligere ex toto corde, tota anima, tota virtute, unum idemque in substantia, distinguat in personis isto ordine vocabulorum.

1099CIpsa vero dilectio hoc ordine distinguitur, ut primo toto corde, deinde tota anima, postremo tota virtute Deus diligatur credendo, tota anima confitendo, tota virtute operando.

In proximi vero dilectione per singula praecepta legalia, quae sequuntur, charitas ordinatur: nam non adulterari, non homicidium facere, non falsum testimonium dicere, honorare patrem et matrem, etc., per ordinem Decalogi, ordinata suo quoque loco charitas est. Quomodo etiam vel quo affectu, diversae in Ecclesia personae diligi debeant, charitas ordinatur, quia alio ordine diligi debet fidelis amicus, alio ordine charissimus filius, alio ordine parentes, alio ordine frater germanus, alio ordine 1099Dconjux, alio ordine a Domino servus, alio ordine a servo Dominus, alio peregrinus, alio agnitus, alio sacerdos, alio propinquus et proximus. Nam largiri necessaria egentibus, visitare infirmos, vel carceri mancipatos, consolari indigentes et injusto judicio oppressos, sepelire mortuos, corrigere prave agentes, adjuvare in aliquo labore fratres, erudire minus scientes, vel si qua alia utilitati proximorum sunt necessaria impendere, omnia profecto sunt ordinabilia sanctae charitatis officia.

Merito ergo mens sancta a rege sponsoque suo in cellam introducitur vinariam, hoc est divinorum praeceptorum intelligentiam, quando dulcedine gratiae ipsius debriata intelligit, tam multipliciter ordinatam impendendae charitatis diligentiam. Unde 1100Acum tanta hujus vini inebriantis fortitudine affectata est, ut ab omni mundana delectatione quasi insensibilis remaneat, et pro immenso taliter ordinatae charitatis desiderio, non tantum obstupescat, sed etiam languescat, quoddam sibi solatium hujus languoris efflagitans subsequitur dicens: Fulcite me floribus, etc.

VERS. 5.-- Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo.

Quid sunt flores, nisi animae boni operis primordia proferentes et coelesti desiderio redolere incipientes? Quid vero sunt mala nisi animae de initiis bonorum operum divinae gratiae nutrimento perfectionem jam tenentes, quasi de floribus ad fructum proficientes? Quae ergo amore divino languet, 1100Bquaerit fulciri floribus, stipari malis, quia cum nondum eum quem tam ordinate toto corde, tota anima, tota virtute, hoc est fide, confessione, operatione diligit, videre sicuti est non praevalet, magna ei tamen consolatio est, quod proximorum nunc inchoantium, nunc perfectorum piis provectibus laetatur.

92 Habet enim sancta Ecclesia quosdam in se minores quos erudiat verbo et exemplo, ut sint quasi flores primitias sanctitatis arripientes. Habet etiam quosdam majores in quibus erudiatur, et quorum doctrinis et exemplis quotidie aedificetur, qui sunt quasi mala maturitate jam et perfectione bonorum operum complacentes. Tales ergo scilicet et minores et majores hujusmodi studio pietatis 1100Csuccrescentes valde sanctam Ecclesiam consolantur, quae certe cum magna laetitia cordis videt, hoc suos filios parvos et magnos, rudes et perfectos diligere quod ipsa vehementer diligit, et haec magna est languoris sui consolatio, in hujus peregrinationis exsilio, ad hoc eos secum ex desiderio tendere, ad quod se credit quandoque ex praemio pervenire.

Hoc etiam modo quilibet sanctus, qui amore Dei languet potest dicere: Fulcite me loribus, stipate me malis, quando magnum hujusmodi languoris aestimat remedium, quod videt in bono opere suorum, quos in Deo diligit, profectum proximorum, horum quidem ad pia studia pullulantium, illorum vero in ipsis studiis fructificantium. Nonne ille qui 1100Dtali amore languebat ut diceret: Cupio dissolvi et esse cum Christo, proximorum tamen utilitatem desiderabat dicens, manere autem in carne necessarium propter vos? (Philipp. I.) Quorum profectum videre pro magna interim reputat consolatione, quando Dei faciem quam tantopere desiderat videre, perfecte praevalet comprehendere. Licet valde cupiat dissolvi et cum Christo esse, nunquid iste qui divino amore languebat, hoc quod amabat, quandoque consequi non posse timebat? Minime; sed hoc dispensatione Dei fiebat, ut hujus praemii dilatio major virtutum fieret exercitatio, amplior quoque pro eorum quos diligebat utilitate, laboris remuneratio, nam qui dissolvi cupiebat utique de praemio certus erat, sicut ipse alibi dicit: Scimus 1101Aquoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod aedificationem ex Deo habemus, domum non manufactam aeternam in coelis (II Cor. V).

Quocirca dilationis hujus poenam levius ferebat, quia eos quos diligebat ad idem praemium percipiendum secum tendere gaudebat.

Unde quibusdam suis discipulis consolatoria mittit, verba dicens: Gratias ago Deo meo semper pro vobis, in gratia Dei quae data est vobis in Christo Jesu, quia in omnibus divites facti estis in illo, in omni verbo et in omni scientia, sicut testimonium Christi confirmatum est in vobis, ita ut nihil desit vobis in ulla gratia, exspectantibus revelationem Domini nostri Jesu Christi (I Cor. I). Ecce qui dissolvi 1101Bet cum Christo esse cupiebat, quantum gaudebat, et gratias agebat, quod quia hoc nondum consequi poterat, filiorum tamen quos in Christo genuerat profectibus, valde hujus dilationis incommodum relevabat.

93 Alio quoque modo, utilitatem et profectum filiorum Ecclesia desiderat per fidem et operationem, ut tunc dicatur fulciri floribus, quando ornatur credentium fide, quae est religionis exordium et quasi primo exsurgens flos sanctitatis. Sed quia fides sine operibus mortua est (Jac. II), stipari dicitur malis, quando ipsorum dicitur credentium multipliciter fructificantium, piis gaudere operibus quasi maturis jam fructibus.

Cumque haec duo ita sibi jungantur, ut altera 1101Csine altera utilis esse non possit; scriptum est enim quia sine fide impossibile est quemquam Deo placere (Hebr. XI), fides autem si non habeat opera, mortua est in semetipsa (Jac. II), magna certe consolatio languentis in amore Dei animae, quando videt proximos proficere fide et operatione.

Verum quoniam haec sponsa Christi quae amore illo tam magnifice, ut diximus, ordinato debilis et languida efficitur, non profectu et utilitate proximorum consolatur, verum etiam re praesentium bonorum et spe futurorum sublevatur, subjungit dicens: Laeva ejus sub capite meo.

VERS. 6.-- Laeva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera ejus amplexabitur me.

1101DLaeva Christi, id est sinistra, sunt bona temporalia, dextera vero ejus bona aeternalia; quaedam autem bona temporalia in hoc mundo pro exspectatione futurorum bonorum Deus suis concedit electis ut dum ejus praesentia munera suscipiunt ardentius et securius ad aeterna appetenda praeparantur.

Sed laeva Christi sub capite ejus est, quia haec ipsa temporalia bona summi amoris intentione premit, ut haec quasi inferiora aspiciat, et aeterna bona semper superiora attendat. Sub capite enim, id est sub mente, non supra debent omnia haec temporalia esse, videlicet ut nunquam ista amori divino praeponat, sed ita eis utatur, ut non ad voluptatem, sed ad necessitatem potius rationabili mentis aequitate 1102Amoderetur et ea magis semper quae supra mentem esse debent, amando et suspirando miretur. Haec est enim dextera ejus quae eum amplexetur, videlicet bona illa perennia, quae eum adepta fuerit, secura beatitudine et beata securitate requiescere possit.

Dicit ergo: Laeva ejus sub capite meo et dextera illius amplexabitur me, quia omnia quae in creaturis ad meam ordinavit utilitatem, habebo in cogitatione pro gratiarum actione, ea vero propter quae haec mihi ad tempus praestita sunt, tota mentis devotione, utpote aeternaliter mecum mansura, diligere et optare studebo.

Sive laeva ejus sub capite meo, quia quod natus et passus est, quod resurrexit et in coelum ascendit, 1102Bin memoria mea erunt; et dextera illius amplexabitur me, quia istorum memoria ad futurae resurrectionis et 94 gloriae insignia, me animabit diligenda et appetenda.

Sive sinistra Dei est ejus in hoc saeculo, parva quaedam cognitio, dextera vero illius, post hanc vitam plenaria et vera ipsius cognitio, sed sinistra sub capite nostro est, dextera vero illius amplexabitur nos, quia videmus nunc quidem per speculum in aenigmate, tunc autem facie ad faciem (I Cor. XIII). Sinistra enim sub capite est quia conceditur nobis in hac vita aliquid de Deo cogitare et mente videre, dextera vero illius amplexabitur nos, quia in futura vita, tanta nos sui complebit et circumdabit visione, ut quale hoc sit, nec oculus videre, 1102Cnec auris audire, nec in cor hominis possit ascendere (I Cor. II).

Haec ergo in sponsa ordinantis gratiae dignatione charitas ordinata capiti laeva supponit et dextera sua eam amplexatur, ut omnibus temporalibus donis secundo loco positis, principaliter in aeternae vitae desiderio requiescat, sitque hoc modo praesentium concessio, etiam futurorum certitudo, mentis in amore Dei debilis et languidae consolatio.

Et vos, dilectae Christo sorores, quae mundum contemnendo amore Dei languetis, tale signum hujusmodi dilectionis dare debetis ut fulcitae sitis floribus credendo, stipatae malis operando. Laeva Christi sit sub capite vestro et dextera illius amplexetur 1102Dvos ut temporalia bona a Deo vobis aliquomodo concessa, quasi inferiora, aeterna vero quasi superiora semper attendatis. Longitudo quippe dierum in dextera ejus, in sinistra ejus divitiae et gloria (Prov. III); quia in hac praesenti vita nonnunquam concedit electis suis divitias bonitatis suae praegustare, in futura vero vita aeternaliter sine fine possidere. Delectationes in dextera ejus sunt usque in finem (Psal. XV), quas profecto adipisci potestis, si in ejus amore ita languetis, ut in eo firmae ac stabilis usque in finem perseveretis. Dextera nempe ejus amplexabitur vos quia non ex parte ut nunc, sed integram et perfectam sui dabit cognitionem et pro brevi et transitorio labore, concedet vobis requiem et vitam et longitudinem dierum in saeculum saeculi. Amen.

CHAPTER TWO.

VERSE 1.-- I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys.

Rightly, he says, O beloved, dost thou judge, who ascribest all thy beauty to me, because I in truth am 1093Dthe flower of the field, that is, the honour and beauty and adornment of the whole universal Church, spread through the whole world, or most joyful field, and diverse in species of holiness and grace, germinating and flowering from my gift. I also am the lily of the valleys, that is, the cleansing, refreshment and medicine of the humble, or of those cast down by some sorrow and affliction of this world for the sake of my name.

85 For the nature of the lily has in it three delightful things: whiteness, odour, medicine against burning; for whoever in this valley of tears, with humbled spirit and contrite heart, bewail their excesses, recognizing themselves infirm and always imploring my aid, without doubt shall obtain cleansing and whiteness of soul, and then 1094Ashall be refreshed by the odour of good conversation, I inspiring and helping, and against all the incentives of the flesh and against the burning of affliction and of the world as it were setting on fire, shall be cooled by the opposing of my love and of the consolation of hope.

Another too, O beloved, I am the flower of the field, that one, namely, of whom Isaiah says: There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root (Isa. XI). For thou didst say above that our bed is flowery, namely the womb of my Mother, from whom I willed to be incarnate; but I say that it is flowery for this reason, because I am its flower, from which flower many other flowers proceed, that is, spiritual grace, which the prophet mentioned enumerates. And there shall rest, he says, upon him, without doubt upon the flower, the spirit of the Lord, the spirit 1094Bof wisdom and of understanding, the spirit of counsel and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and of piety, and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him (ibid.). I am the flower, then, of the field, namely of that earth of which it is said: Truth is sprung out of the earth (Psal. LXXXIV); which is therefore called a field, because it is not rough, nor tortuous, a village, but level and even, as being levelled by the power of the Most High after the manner of a plain from every unevenness of morals; which brought me forth, the flower of flowers, that is, the Holy of holies, without the seed of man, just as a field without seed produces the shoots of diverse flowers and herbs.

The lily too am I of the valleys, that is, the whiteness and odour and salvation of those who imitate the humility of my mother, and not of those who glory in the merit of chastity; for those who glory, and contain themselves for human favour only, 1094Chave not progress, the lily of virginal whiteness, and, by inward purity, the sign; but rather they are unclean with the blackness of vainglory before the sight of my purity, and therefore I neither am nor can be called their lily: but of those who imitate me and her, I am the lily by the gift of grace, she is the lily by example, so that they too may become a lily by imitation. Whence follows: as the lily among thorns.

VERSE 2.-- As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

As I, he says, among the Jews, whom I expected to make grapes, but they made thorns (Isa. V), shone with humility, meekness, patience and the manifold grace of the virtues, while they, standing like a thorn against 1094Dme, pricked me with many stings of words and of manners, so thou, O my Church, my bride, or any soul whatever that loves me, you ought to be among the daughters 86 of this world, that is, souls thorny with malice and unbelief, in humility and patience, so that, when thou hast imitated me in this manner, thou mayest be proved truly my love, and let such imitation of me be the proof of true friendship.

Or as my mother according to the flesh, Mary, who is a lily by the whiteness of virginity and the odour of holiness, went her way with humility and patience among the daughters of the Synagogue, who like thorns pricked her, putting upon her the stain of infamy, because they did not believe in the virtue and power of God. Because she recognized through the spirit the dispensation of God, and felt fulfilled in herself what she had formerly heard through the prophet and afterwards through the angel. 1095ASo also, by her example, whatever soul is a friend to me through faith and love ought, among the daughters whom the corruption of malice and impiety has begotten, to keep humility, patience and honesty, and on account of the hope of future remuneration never to fall away from them.

Or let us say simply that the soul which wishes to show itself worthy of the friendship of God ought always to stand among depraved men as the lily among liliuminter thorns, so that, as the lily among thorns, being set there, does not lose the dignity of its whiteness and odour, so she, among depraved manners, may not lose the integrity of faith and patience, or of any holiness granted her, but rather may learn by tolerating that, the more she is afflicted by their perversity, so much the more are the merits of greater virtues heaped up for her; 1095Bfor, as blessed Gregory says, whoever does not tolerate the wicked, he himself through his intolerance is witness to thee that he is not good. Hence blessed Job speaks of himself, saying: A brother am I of dragons and a companion of ostriches (Job XXX); and the Lord to Ezekiel: The sons of man are unbelievers and subverters with thee, thou dwellest with scorpions [Vulg. Ez 2:6 fili hominis … increduli et subversores sunt tecum, "O son of man … unbelievers and subverters are with thee"] (Ezech. II). Peter also approves the life of Lot, saying: And he delivered just Lot, oppressed by the injury and the luxurious conversation of the wicked; for in sight and hearing he was just: dwelling among them who from day to day vexed the soul of the just man with wicked works (II Petr. II). Hence John writes to the Church of Pergamum, saying: I know where thou dwellest, where the seat of Satan is, and thou hast my name, and hast not denied my faith (Apoc. II); Paul also 1095Cpraises and strengthens his disciples, saying: In the midst of a depraved and perverse nation, among whom you shine as lights in the world. Holding the word of life (Philip. II).

By these authorities it is sufficiently established how great a virtue it is to tolerate the depraved manners of men, since from the greater malice of the reprobate greater gains of merits grow for the elect, because it is written: The more Pharaoh oppressed the people of God, the more it was multiplied (Exod. I).

But who the daughters are among whom the Church or holy soul is said to dwell as the lily among thorns is gathered from the comparison itself, because as for those which are compared to thorns, it is evident 87 that they are taken in the adverse part; and they are therefore called daughters, because 1095Dthey are generated from the wicked seed of perverse doctrine, or from an evil conception of the mind. But the Church, or any faithful soul whatever, which through faith and operation is the bride of Christ, that she may be able to be as the lily among thorns, comes to meet him who rules and protects her with gracious praise through another comparison, saying: As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, etc.

VERSE 3.-- As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. Under the shadow of him whom I had desired I sat, and his fruit was sweet to my throat.

My beloved, she says, has compared me to the lily among thorns, keeping its virtue, which, although he has granted it me by his gift, yet he taught me by his own example that I should become this. For as the apple tree, fruit-bearing, having in itself three useful things by which it refreshes, 1096Athis being fruit, odour and shade, among the trees of the woods too, which certainly are unfruitful, is held incomparable, so my beloved, by the fruit and odour of holiness and of justice and of doctrine, and by the shade of his protection, with which he refreshes, teaches and defends those who believe in him, among the sons, that is, the Jews, stood forth; who at first indeed were sons, and now wish to be, but are not, because of them God said: I have nourished and exalted sons, but they have despised me (Isa. I); and elsewhere: The strange sons have lied to me, the strange sons have grown old and have halted from their paths (Psal. XVII): who boast themselves to be sons of Abraham, but are not, because they have not the works (Joan. VIII); and therefore they are unfruitful and useless trees, and on this account to be cut down and cast into the fire. For among such 1096Btrees, caught by eternal burning, he hung on the tree of the cross, from which he poured out for me the sweetest fruit of his body and blood, with which he daily refreshes those who believe in him: but they, like wild trees, not only brought forth no fruit of good work, but even poured out the most bitter sap of their malice and impiety, crying: Crucify, crucify (Joan. XIX.), and: His blood be upon us and upon our sons (Matth. XVII).

Under the shade of this tree, then, that is, the refreshment and consoling defence of the New Testament, which I was desiring now for a long time in the ancient fathers, who sighed with great desire for the times of softening and refreshing grace, now at length after the advent, passion, resurrection and ascension of Christ 1096CI sat, with faith unshaken and stable. For the Law, with a certain heat of inclemency and of incurable punishment, when it said: If anyone shall have done this or that, let him die the death (Exod. XIX), had long afflicted me; but grace moved such heat with the shade of mercy and the remedy of penance, under which desirable shade I did not walk, did not stand, but rather sat and rested, because 88 I received this decree of piety, confirmed by the authority of my Lord himself, to be held immutably.

This tree indeed is the tree of life, whose shade and divine protection, which its branches pour out, branches of honour and grace, which namely are the oppositions of diverse virtues against the heats of worldly temptations: as, against pride, 1096Dthe opposition of humility is necessary; against anger, of patience; against lust, of chastity and continence; against contumacy, of obedience; against avarice, of largesse and mercy; against strifes and contentions, of peace and concord; against envy and hatred, of love; and that we may comprehend it briefly, against all the delights and temptations of this world surely there must be opposed the remembrance of the future misery of the wicked and the glory of the just.

The outpourings of such shades indeed protect the soul from the heat of carnal suggestions and delights, under which, because I desired them, I sat, that is, I rested, since indeed I found in them the grateful and wholesome refreshment of protecting grace.

And his fruit, without doubt that of that apple tree, 1097Athat is, of Christ, my bridegroom and Lord, sweet to my throat, because the utility and suavity of his precepts is sweet and pleasing to the palate of my heart and to the capacity of my mind. Or the fruit of this apple tree hanging on the tree of the cross is sweet to my throat, because the receiving of the body and blood of Christ pours sweetness and health into my breast, and it is plainly the perfect refection of my body and soul ani mae.

Otherwise also the sons among whom the bridegroom is said to dwell as the apple tree among the trees of the woods are taken to be the elect, who are called sons of God by name, on account of the observance of his commandments, for which they shall obtain from their heavenly Father himself the inheritance of eternal life; among whom Christ dwells like the apple tree among the trees of the woods, because as the apple tree 1097Bexcels all the trees of the woods in beauty and in the odour and sweetness of its fruits, so Christ goes before all the saints in the comeliness of virtues and the sweetness of doctrine, as it is written of him: Beautiful in form above the sons of men, grace is poured abroad in thy lips; therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows (Psal. XLIV).

Under whose shade or the Church, because, the branches of that tree, whether of sacraments, or of commandments, or of gifts, being spread through the whole breadth of the world, she is wonderfully protected and consoled from all heat of sadness and perturbation, remaining secure and immovable through the hope of future retribution, whose fruit is sweet to the throat of her, because all the mystical things of his utterances, and the venerable institutions of the sacraments, which 1097Che brought forth from the hidden wisdom of his divinity, are sweet and pleasing to the mind that devoutly embraces and venerates them, 89 on account of the salvation which is conferred on it from thence, quickening and refreshing without end.

But what effect the sweetness and suavity of this fruit has, what more sublime and more perfect thing it brings forth, she shows by what she adds.

VERSE 4.-- The king hath brought me into the wine-cellar, he hath set in order charity in me. [Vulg. Ct 2:4 Introduxit me in cellam vinariam, without rex, "the king"]

The effect of this introduction proceeded from the cause of the fruit, well pleasing and therefore taken up with great zeal of mind, because the more the precepts of God are desired, so much the more fully are they admitted by divine love to ever greater things to be desired. That fruit indeed 1097Dwhich flowed forth, and still flows forth, from that glorious and most excellent tree, the Lord Jesus Christ, not all receive equally: because one receives this, another that, according to what he savours and loves.

For to this one the virtue of patience savours and pleases more, to that one, of obedience; to this one, of humility, to that one, of continence; this one the assiduity of prayer delights more, that one, of reading, of fasts; and in the whole they procure by divine gift the species of the virtues, of the graces.

But there is a certain as it were singular and as it were separate storehouse, standing in a certain secret place, which is called a cell because of a certain narrowness of its own, in that it admits few into its recesses, where is laid up the sweetness and suavity of that fruit which maketh glad the heart of man (Psal. CIII), and boils out every humour of vices, 1098Anamely the evangelical precept concerning the utility of charity. Which is rightly called by the name of wine, because as wine, by purging itself, rejects from itself everything pestiferous, and by its natural colour boils out every noxious humour; so the precept of charity puts to flight from the heart every pest of vices, and expels all the passions of the mind, because no one can both have charity and be evil; and therefore the full understanding of this is deservedly called the wine-cellar.

Those, then, who delight to rest under the branches of that saving tree and to gather without loathing the sweetest fruit of holiness, will at some time arrive at this perfection, that they enter the wine-cellar without obstacle, because this way is not narrow for them, for whom the way of worldly pleasure, 1098Bbroad and spacious, is utterly closed. For the way of this precept is narrow, because it seems difficult to many and laborious when it is said: Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you (Matth. V).

But because we read that it has been observed by many saints, this precept is not difficult except to those who have not yet perfectly tasted the sweetness of the fruits, that is, of the divine commandments. This, then, is the wine-cellar, perfection, and, to those freely entering the narrow way, sweetly savouring and on this account perfectible, of the understanding of the divine precept concerning the excellence of charity.

But because charity itself looks in diverse directions, there is necessary in it 90 an order to be attended to, so that one may know in what place each affection is to be put, and which is to be taken as prior, which as posterior. Whence, when she had set before: 1098CThe king hath brought me into the wine-cellar, she adds, and he hath set in order charity in me. For this is the order of holy love, that first we love God, then our neighbour, lastly even the enemy himself. This order is indeed necessary, because it is impossible that anyone love his neighbour, or, what is more difficult, his enemy, unless he love God, since the cause of the love of these is the love of God, and in this way what was impossible becomes possible. For what is necessary to be, it is impossible not to be, and what is necessary not to be, it is impossible to be. But it is necessary that the love of God be where the love of neighbour is, because no one loves his neighbour for God's sake unless he love God: but it is necessary that the love of God not be where 1098Dthe love of neighbour is not, according to the word of John: He that loveth not his brother whom he saw, God whom he seeth not, how can he love? (I Joan. IV.) But it is not always necessary that the love of God not be where the love of the enemy is not, because it can happen that one who loves God has no enemy whom he may love for God's sake: but if he has one, then it is necessary that the love of God not be where the love of the enemy is not, because he proves that he does not love God who is unwilling to love his enemy for God's sake.

This order, then, as has been said, seems to be necessary, when it is determined that love of neighbour is impossible unless the love of God precede, according, however, to that love which is according to God, not that which is according to the world. For the love 1099Aof the world is without the love of God, because that is according to the flesh, this according to the spirit.

But the mode of love according to the flesh is twofold: one which is altogether against God, as is that of the wicked who love one another for the fellowship of iniquity; the other which is not against God, as is that of parents, kinsmen, and friends, to which love, however, the love of God is always to be preferred, and, for God's sake, the love of each neighbour. But the first mode according to the flesh is altogether foreign to the present place, because it is wholly disordered and contrary to God; but the other, which is not against God, is not abhorrent to the present place, if only it be ordered, because if a man is loved more in God than God, then it is disordered.

1099BIt may, however, not absurdly be taken so that we say that the order of charity is twofold, one in God, the other in the neighbour: for it is written: God is charity (I Joan. IV): and in this charity which is God, the Church, or any holy soul whatever, ought to learn, know and understand the order, that in the first place she should name the Father as the voice, in the second the Son as the word from the voice, in the third the Holy Spirit as the reason proceeding from the voice and the word. But let her not say it in that sense, as though there were any degree in the Trinity, 91 which it is impious to say, but that she may distinguish in persons, by this order of terms, that charity, that is, God, whom she ought to love with the whole heart, the whole soul, the whole strength, one and the same in substance.

1099CBut love itself is distinguished by this order, that God be loved first with the whole heart, then with the whole soul, lastly with the whole strength, by believing, with the whole soul by confessing, with the whole strength by working.

But in the love of neighbour charity is ordered through the several precepts of the Law which follow: for not to commit adultery, not to do murder, not to speak false witness, to honour father and mother, etc., following the order of the Decalogue, is charity ordered, each in its own place as well. How also, or with what affection, the diverse persons in the Church ought to be loved, charity is ordered; because in one order ought the faithful friend to be loved, in another order the dearest son, in another order parents, in another order the full brother, in another order 1099Dthe spouse, in another order the servant by the master, in another order the master by the servant, in another the stranger, in another the acquaintance, in another the priest, in another the kinsman and neighbour. For to bestow necessaries on the needy, to visit the sick or those committed to prison, to console the needy and those oppressed by unjust judgment, to bury the dead, to correct those who act wickedly, to help brothers in some labour, to instruct the less knowing, or to expend whatever other things are necessary to the utility of neighbours, all these assuredly are orderable offices of holy charity.

Deservedly, then, the holy mind is brought in by her king and bridegroom into the wine-cellar, that is, into the understanding of the divine precepts, when, inebriated by the sweetness of his grace, she understands the diligence of charity to be expended, so manifoldly ordered. Whence, 1100Awhen she is affected by so great a strength of this inebriating wine that she remains as it were insensible to every worldly delight, and for the immense desire of charity so ordered is not only stupefied but even languishes, demanding for herself some solace of this languor, she goes on to say: Stay me up with flowers, etc.

VERSE 5.-- Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples, because I languish with love.

What are the flowers but souls bringing forth the beginnings of good work and beginning to be fragrant with heavenly desire? And what are the apples but souls already holding perfection from the beginnings of good works through the nourishment of divine grace, as it were advancing from flowers to fruit? She, then, who languishes with divine love 1100Bseeks to be stayed up with flowers, compassed about with apples, because, since she is not yet able to see as he is him whom she loves so orderly with the whole heart, the whole soul, the whole strength, that is, with faith, confession, operation, yet it is a great consolation to her that she rejoices in the pious advancements of her neighbours, now beginning, now perfected.

92 For holy Church has in herself certain lesser ones whom she may instruct by word and example, that they may be as flowers catching the first-fruits of holiness. She has also certain greater ones in whom she may be instructed, and by whose doctrines and examples she may be daily edified, who are as apples, pleasing already by the maturity and perfection of good works. Such, then, namely both the lesser and the greater, growing up in this manner with zeal for piety, 1100Cgreatly console holy Church, which surely with great gladness of heart sees her sons, small and great, rude and perfect, love this which she herself vehemently loves; and this is a great consolation of her languor, in the exile of this pilgrimage, that they tend with her by desire towards that to which she believes she will at some time arrive by reward.

In this way too any saint whatever who languishes with the love of God can say: Stay me up with flowers loribus, compass me about with apples, when he esteems as a great remedy of such languor the progress of his neighbours, which he sees in the good work of his own, whom he loves in God, these indeed sprouting towards pious pursuits, those bearing fruit in those very pursuits. Did not he who 1100Dlanguished with such love that he said: I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, nevertheless desire the utility of his neighbours, saying, but to remain in the flesh is necessary for your sakes? (Philipp. I.) Whose progress to see he meanwhile reckons as a great consolation, when he is perfectly able [praevalet; read non praevalet, "is not able"] to comprehend the face of God which he so greatly desires to see. Although he greatly desires to be dissolved and to be with Christ, did he who languished with divine love fear that he could not at some time attain what he loved? By no means; but this came about by the dispensation of God, that the delay of this reward might become a greater exercise of virtues, and also an ampler remuneration of labour for the utility of those whom he loved; for he who desired to be dissolved was certainly sure of the reward, as he himself says elsewhere: We know 1101Athat if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens (II Cor. V).

Wherefore he bore the pain of this delay more lightly, because he rejoiced that those whom he loved were tending with him to receive the same reward.

Whence he sends consolatory things to certain of his disciples, saying words: I give thanks to my God always for you, in the grace of God which is given you in Christ Jesus, because in all things you are made rich in him, in all utterance and in all knowledge, as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you, so that nothing is wanting to you in any grace, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ (I Cor. I). Behold, he who desired to be dissolved 1101Band to be with Christ, how much he rejoiced and gave thanks, that, because he could not yet attain this, yet by the advancements of the sons whom he had begotten in Christ he greatly relieved the inconvenience of this delay.

93 In another way also the Church desires the utility and progress of her sons through faith and operation, so that she is then said to be stayed up with flowers when she is adorned with the faith of believers, which is the beginning of religion and as it were the first rising flower of holiness. But because faith without works is dead (Jac. II), she is said to be compassed about with apples when she is said to rejoice in the pious works of those same believers, bearing fruit manifoldly, as in fruits already ripe.

And since these two are so joined to each other that the one 1101Ccannot be useful without the other; for it is written that without faith it is impossible for anyone to please God (Hebr. XI), but faith, if it have not works, is dead in itself (Jac. II), great surely is the consolation of the soul languishing in the love of God when she sees her neighbours advance in faith and operation.

But since this bride of Christ, who by that love so magnificently, as we have said, ordered is made weak and languid, is not [non; read non solum, "not only"] consoled by the progress and utility of her neighbours, but is also lifted up by the reality of present goods and the hope of future ones, she adds, saying: His left hand under my head.

VERSE 6.-- His left hand under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

1101DThe left hand of Christ, that is, the sinistra, are temporal goods, but his right hand eternal goods; but certain temporal goods in this world God grants to his elect for the expectation of future goods, so that while they receive his present gifts they may be prepared more ardently and more securely for desiring the eternal.

But the left hand of Christ is under the head of her, because she presses down these very temporal goods by the intention of the highest love, so that she may look upon them as lower, and always attend to eternal goods as higher. For under the head, that is, under the mind, not above, ought all these temporal things to be, namely that she may never set them before divine love, but may so use them that, not for pleasure but rather for necessity, she may moderate them by the reasonable equity of the mind 1102Aand may always admire the more, by loving and sighing, those things which ought to be above the mind. For this is his right hand which may embrace him, namely those everlasting goods, which, when she shall have obtained him, she may be able to rest in secure blessedness and blessed security.

She says, therefore: His left hand under my head and his right hand shall embrace me, because all things that he has ordered in creatures for my utility I shall hold in thought for thanksgiving, but those on account of which these things have been furnished me for a time, as being to abide with me eternally, I shall be zealous to love and to desire with the whole devotion of my mind.

Or, his left hand under my head, because that he was born and suffered, that he rose again and ascended into heaven, 1102Bwill be in my memory; and his right hand shall embrace me, because the memory of these things will animate me to the ensigns of the future resurrection and 94 glory, to be loved and desired.

Or the left hand of God is, in this world, a certain small knowledge of him, but the right hand of him, after this life, the full and true knowledge of him; but the left hand under our head is, but the right hand of him shall embrace us, because we see now indeed through a glass in a dark manner, but then face to face (I Cor. XIII). For the left hand is under the head because it is granted to us in this life to think something of God and to see it with the mind, but the right hand of him shall embrace us, because in the future life he will fill and surround us with so great a vision of himself that what this may be neither eye can see, 1102Cnor ear hear, nor into the heart of man can it ascend (I Cor. II).

This charity, then, ordered in the bride by the condescension of ordering grace, sets the left hand under her head and embraces her with its right hand, so that, all temporal gifts being put in the second place, she may rest principally in the desire of eternal life; and that in this way the grant of present things may be also the certainty of future things, the consolation of the mind weak and languid in the love of God.

And you, sisters beloved of Christ, who by despising the world languish with the love of God, ought to give such a sign of this kind of love that you may be stayed up with flowers by believing, compassed about with apples by working. Let the left hand of Christ be under your head and his right hand embrace 1102Dyou, so that you may always attend to the temporal goods somehow granted you by God as lower, but to the eternal as higher. For length of days is in his right hand, in his left hand riches and glory (Prov. III); because in this present life he sometimes grants to his elect to foretaste the riches of his goodness, but in the future life to possess them eternally without end. Delights in the right hand of him are even unto the end (Psal. XV), which you can surely obtain, if you so languish in his love that you persevere in him firm and stable even unto the end. His right hand indeed shall embrace you, because not in part as now, but whole and perfect knowledge of himself he will give, and for brief and transitory labour he will grant you rest and life and length of days for ever and ever. Amen.

LIBER SECUNDUS.

BOOK TWO.

95 PROOEMIUM.

  • 1103A

Quomodo, inquit Psalmista, cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena? (Psal. CXXXVI.) Quid vero est canticum Domini? Primo, ut simpliciter dicamus: Canticum Domini est quidquid secundum ecclesiasticae doctrinae vel sanctionis modum concordi modulatione sensuum et verborum componimus, scribimus et dicimus. Canticum Domini est tota Veteris et Novi Testamenti pagina, quam bene decantamus quando hanc recta et plena fide annuntiamus, nunc rerum gestarum seriem, nunc ipsarum rerum significationem in Domini exponentes laudem. Sed hujusmodi Canticum potest quilibet cantare per modum scientiae non tantum in sua, sed etiam in aliena terra; quia non aufert locus corporalis 1103Bpotestatem cantandi, licet auferat voluntatem et voluptatem, propter aliquam tristitiae passionem: sicut illi populo in captivitatis moerore constituto, quibus cum diceretur: Hymnum cantate nobis de canticis Sion, responderunt: Quomodo cantabimus canticum Domini in terra aliena? Siquidem ut in figura accipiamus, illorum non posse cantare canticum Domini in terra aliena, fuit nos non posse Dominum perfecte laudare in loco peregrinationis nostrae; quae est nobis quasi terra aliena; Quia non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus (Hebr. XIII), quae est patria nostra et terra aeternae haereditatis nostrae. Nam Dei opera narrare, mandata ejus edicere, scribere et exponere, est, ut diximus, quoddam canticum Domini 1103Ccantare: hoc etiam possibile in isto loco peregrinationis nostrae, dum dicat Psalmista: Cantabiles mihi erant justificationes tuae in loco peregrinationis meae (Psal. CXVIII).

Verum ut altius aliquid consideremus, est et aliud canticum Domini, quod non est possibile in terra aliena cantare. Quodnam vero est illud? Nimirum quod modulatur Spiritus sanctus sua septiformi gratia, quasi per septem vocum discrimina; quia aliter resonat vox illa interioris hominis per spiritum sapientiae, aliter per spiritum intellectus, aliter per spiritum consilii atque aliter per spiritum fortitudinis; alio vero modo per spiritum scientiae et alio per spiritum pietatis, alio quoque 1103Dper spiritum Domini (Isa. XI).

His enim gratiarum distributionibus, quasi quibusdam diversis vocibus constituitur tota modulatio, cantici 96 Domini, cantici illius dulcissimi, quae canit virtutum fidibus, vita honesta, sancta, Deo placens et perfecta.

Nulla quippe ibi est dissonantia inter carnem et spiritum quia tam concorditer succinit caro spiritui ut perfectam construant harmoniam spiritualis 1104Acantici, quod est in loco peregrinationis nostrae optimum genus cantici divini. Sed istud canticum non potest cantari in terra aliena, hoc est in corpore subdito peccatis; quod tunc est terra aliena, quando peccando existens in potestate diaboli indignum est habitatione Christi: sive a nobis tunc alienatur quando spiritui et mentis rationi male agens reluctatur. Aliena est terra. Homo terrena semper diligendo, et ob hoc alienus a Deo, atque ideo impotens cantare canticum Domini, quia animalis homo non percipit quae sunt Spiritus Dei (I Cor. II).

Sed quorum ista? Ad hoc plane ut ostendam vobis, sanctissimae sorores, supra vires meas esse hoc quod mihi injunxistis officium, quia dum nihil 1104Baut parum aptus sim cantare Canticum Domini, longe minus aptus ero cantare Canticum Domini canticorum. Hujusmodi enim materia debet esse oratorum eloquenter et sapienter declamantium quorum est officium dicere apposite ad persuadendum, finis vero persuadere dictione, sed cum in me sint neque sapientia neque eloquentia, cui deest officium apposite dicendi, minus profecto adest finis dictione persuadendi. Tunc enim vobis utiliter scriberem si ea quae dico vel dicturus sum ita apposite dicerem, ut vobis ad vitae honestatem et animae utilitatem persuadere possem. Nam terra mea aliena est, repugnans spiritui serviens Domino peccati, atque ideo non sum idoneus in ea cantare Canticum Domini, quanto minus 1104CCantica canticorum. Sed ut quidam fuit, liceat sperare timenti, ut qui prae parvitate sensus mei tam sublimem materiam timeo prosequi, sperem tamen per orationes vestras ad ea quae coepi exsequenda pro divinitatis respectu adjuvari.

95 PROEM.

  • 1103A

How, says the Psalmist, shall we sing the canticle of the Lord in a strange land? (Psal. CXXXVI.) But what is the canticle of the Lord? First, to speak simply: The canticle of the Lord is whatever we compose, write and say according to the manner of the Church's doctrine or ordinance, in a concordant modulation of senses and words. The canticle of the Lord is the whole page of the Old and New Testament, which we sing well when we announce it with right and full faith, setting forth to the praise of the Lord now the series of the things done, now the signification of the things themselves. But a Canticle of this kind anyone can sing by way of knowledge, not only in his own land but also in a strange land; because a bodily place does not take away 1103Bthe power of singing, though it may take away the will and the pleasure, because of some passion of sadness: as with that people set in the grief of captivity, who, when it was said to them, Sing us a hymn from the canticles of Sion, answered: How shall we sing the canticle of the Lord in a strange land? For, to take it in figure, their not being able to sing the canticle of the Lord in a strange land was our not being able to praise the Lord perfectly in the place of our pilgrimage; which is to us as it were a strange land; Because we have not here a lasting city, but we seek one to come (Hebr. XIII), which is our fatherland and the land of our eternal inheritance. For to tell the works of God, to declare his commandments, to write and expound them, is, as we have said, to sing a certain canticle of the Lord 1103C: this too is possible in this place of our pilgrimage, since the Psalmist says: Thy justifications were the subject of my song in the place of my pilgrimage (Psal. CXVIII).

But that we may consider something higher, there is also another canticle of the Lord, which it is not possible to sing in a strange land. And which is that? Surely the one which the Holy Spirit modulates by his sevenfold grace, as it were through the distinctions of seven voices; because that voice of the inner man sounds in one way through the spirit of wisdom, in another through the spirit of understanding, in another through the spirit of counsel, and in another through the spirit of fortitude; but in another manner through the spirit of knowledge, and in another through the spirit of piety, and in another again 1103Dthrough the spirit of the Lord (Isa. XI).

For by these distributions of graces, as by certain different voices, is constituted the whole modulation, of the canticle 96 of the Lord, of that most sweet canticle, which a life honest, holy, pleasing to God and perfect sings on the strings of the virtues.

For there is no dissonance there between flesh and spirit, because the flesh sings in accord with the spirit so concordantly that they build up the perfect harmony of the spiritual 1104Acanticle, which is, in the place of our pilgrimage, the best kind of divine canticle. But this canticle cannot be sung in a strange land, that is, in a body subject to sins; which is then a strange land when, being by sinning in the power of the devil, it is unworthy of the dwelling of Christ: or it is then estranged from us when, doing ill, it struggles against the spirit and the reason of the mind. Strange is the land. Man by always loving earthly things, and on this account estranged from God, and therefore powerless to sing the canticle of the Lord, because the sensual man perceiveth not the things that are of the Spirit of God (I Cor. II).

But to what purpose are these things? Plainly to this, that I may show you, most holy sisters, that this office which you have enjoined on me is beyond my strength, because while I am not at all 1104Bor but little fit to sing the Canticle of the Lord, far less fit shall I be to sing the Canticle of the Lord of canticles. For matter of this kind ought to belong to orators declaiming eloquently and wisely, whose office is to speak aptly for persuading, and whose end is to persuade by speech; but since there is in me neither wisdom nor eloquence, in one who lacks the office of speaking aptly, still less assuredly is the end of persuading by speech present. For I should then be writing to you profitably if I were saying the things I say or am about to say so aptly that I could persuade you to honesty of life and profit of soul. For my land is a strange land, resisting the spirit, serving the Lord of sin, and therefore I am not fit to sing in it the Canticle of the Lord, how much less 1104Cthe Canticles of canticles. But as a certain one was, let it be permitted to one who fears to hope, so that I, who for the smallness of my understanding fear to pursue so sublime a matter, may yet hope through your prayers to be helped, out of regard for the Divinity, in carrying through the things I have begun.

SEQUITUR CAPUT II.

VERS. 7.-- Adjuro vos, filiae Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit.

Igitur dilectus dilectae delectatus dormitione, cujus capiti, id est menti sinistram suam, hoc est temporalem utilitatem supposuerat, dextra vero sua, hoc est aeternae vitae dilectione amplexatus fuerat, taliter filias Jerusalem, hoc est animas fideles 1104Dalloquitur, dicens: Adjuro vos, filiae Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit.

Quae est ista tam suavis tamque salubris dormitio ut propter eam talis fiat dilecti adjuratio! Nonne illa est in qua dulci et optabili quiete dilecta requiescens supra dixerat, laeva ejus sub capite meo et dextera illius amplexabitur me?

97 Omnia enim temporalia postposuerat, 1105Aaeternalia vero et indeficientia bona illo contemplatorio concupiscibilis animae oculo intendebat et in hac desiderabili mentis visione delectabiliter quasi dormiebat. Non enim potest leviter hujusmodi provenire dormitio in mente jam omnibus actis exoccupata et magna sibi quiete in amore Dei constrata. Unde per Psalmistam monens Dominus: Vacate, inquit, et videte quoniam ego sum Deus (Psal. XLV). Duae istae dictiones in hoc proposito sunt inseparabiles, quia nequaquam poterit quispiam intimae contemplationis oculo Deitatis essentiam videre, nisi prius studuerit ab omni exteriori impedimento vacare: praemisso ergo vacate, subdit videte, quatenus insinuet prius vacandum in mente, ab omni mundanarum rerum cogitatione ut inde 1105Bfiat possibile, quasi clauso in terrenis oculo perspicatiori et subtiliori visione in divinitatis amore dormire.

Sed cum non sit aequaliter adveniens et manens hujus dormitionis gratia, quando constat alium majori, alium minori contemplationis virtute sublevari (plus enim Maria Petro vel Joanne, isti autem plus alio quolibet sancto in divina profecerunt visione): certum est, diverso sanctos quosque modo dormitionis hujus habere sanctitatem, multiplicem propter quietis disparitatem, ut suo quisque loco juxta collatam sibi quietis gratiam, specialem in contemplativa vita habeat dormitionem. Unde propheta in persona uniuscujusque fidelis hoc modo dormientis dicit: Quiescam et considerabo 1105Cin loco meo (Isa. XVIII): ac si patenter dicat: Quia iste est ordo dormitionis ut non liceat prius dormire quam quietem habere; quiescam, hoc est omnis a me terrenae sollicitudinis causas auferam, et tunc demum mente ab his dormiendo divinae contemplationis adhaerebo in loco collatae mihi specialiter gratiae. Hoc ergo quocunque modo vel loco dormiente dilecta, adjurantur a dilecto filiae Jerusalem, ne suscitent eam neque evigilare faciant, quoad ipsa velit.

Quae vero sunt filiae Jerusalem nisi animae ad supernae pacis visionem tendentes, sed adhuc praepudiente mentis infirmitate minus pervenire valentes?

Quid autem dilecti est adjuvare, nisi praeceptorum 1105Dsuorum decretali conscripto obligare? Porro ipsa praecepta quae sunt, nisi veluti capreae cervique camporum ad coelestia sublevantes alacresque et fortes in bono opere facientes, doctrinae sanctarum Scripturarum.

Sive per capreas et cervos intelligere possumus Patres veteris et novi Testamenti quorum ingenia, virtutes et studia naturali gestione denotantur. Quatuor enim naturae notabilia dicitur habere capreas quod cum vulnerata fuerit gustato 98 dictamno sanatur, quod herbas salubres visus acumine discernit, quod ruminat, quod in montuosis pascitur et semper altiora petit. Et haec est vita et doctrina sanctorum, excessus suos humili 1106Aconfessione sanare, sententias meliores sanctarum Scripturarum sensus sui acumine discernere, divinorum mandatorum cibaria legendo sumere et tenaci memoriae commendando resumere, de virtutibus, ad virtutes profectu quotidiano assurgere.

In cervo quoque tria attenduntur naturae probabilia, quod scilicet serpentem deglutiens potato fonte cum pilis totius corporis omne venenum deponit; quod a canibus agitatus in densissimis silvis viam sibi fugiendi cornibus aperit; quod in mutandis pascuis facto agmine alter alterius dorso capite imposito invicem propter pondus cornuum sustentantur.

Haec quoque fidelibus convenit agere et docere, ut qui aliquo peccati veneno infectus fuerit, ad fontem 1106Bmisericordiae Christum recurrat, cujus pietatis et gratiae infusione, possit et illo peccato, et caeteris animi vitiis carere. Si a malignis spiritibus veluti quibusdam canibus in silvis saecularium negotiorum, quae plena sunt peccatis et vitiis, animo agitatur, viam sibi aufugiendi ea faciat forti repulsione spiritus sive abrenuntiatis omnibus hujusmodi occupationibus soli Deo vacare studeat in contemplativae vitae amore, quod est etiam cornibus viam sibi salutis aperire. Cornu quippe cum de carne nascatur, carnem excedit, et ille qui contemplativae vitae inhaeret, quamvis in carne sit, extra carnem tamen mente sublevatur. Infirmitates morum sive corporum studeant invicem aequanimiter tolerare, et officiosa sibi obsequi charitate; sicut 1106Cdicit Apostolus: Alter alterius onera portate et sic adimplebitis legem Christi (Gal. VI).

Adjurantur ergo a sponso filiae Jerusalem, hoc est obligantur animae pacem sequi cupientes, per capreas cervosque camporum, hoc est per praecepta et documenta sanctorum Patrum, ne suscitent neque evigilare faciant dilectam, hoc est ne inquietent a proposito hujus intimae quietis et dormitionis; donec ipsa velit, hoc est donec ei aspiret ille ejus intimus habitator, cui per amorem colligatur ut velit proximorum infirmitati interdum condescendere, et eorum necessariis utilitatibus providere. Hoc enim velle in ejus cuncta providentis est dispositione qui ei per occultam inspirationem manifestat, 1106Dquando sit utile et honestum contemplationi inhaerere et quando proximorum necessitatibus providere 99 pro loco et tempore.

Denique hujus admirationis talis est vis, qua constringuntur filii obedientiae, ut exhibeant praelatis suis honestatem reverentiae, quia scriptum est: Obedite praepositis vestris et subjacete eis, ipsi enim pervigilant quasi rationem reddituri pro animabus vestris (Hebr. XIII). Inde est quod non audent eos suscitare quasi vicarios Christi officio, sponsus vero sanctae conversationis studio ne perturbent eos, si compellent eos aliqua sui improbitate, sive importunitate ab internae quietis secreto avelli et frequentius exterioribus occupari. Ipsi quoque subjecti hujus admirationis verbum inter se invicem 1107Asuscipere debent, ne pia fratrum studia inquietent sive in lectione, sive in oratione, sive in aliquo spirituali officio quandiu eos in hoc detinet Divinitatis inspiratio.

Verum hujus contemplatoriae dormitionis quietem dilecta semper flagrans, gaudeat se confirmari et defendi tali adjuramento dilecti et quasi jure non debeat inquietari, securior facta proclamat: Vox dilecti mei.

VERS. 8.-- Vox dilecti mei, ecce iste venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles.

Vox, inquit, praedictae admirationis non est vox alicujus prophetae, non legislatoris, non doctoris, quasi ex semetipso aliquid annuntiantis vel docentis; sed potius ipsius dilecti, et per se ipsum; et 1107Bper eos mysteriorum et mandatorum suorum decreta constituentis, quia omnis Scriptura dilecti mei vox est spiritu oris ejus prolata, et divinitatis ipsius digito in cordibus nostris descripta. Et ideo hanc vocem non parvi pendere debetis, filiae Jerusalem, ut me causa rerum exteriorum suscitetis et frequentius evigilare cogatis.

Nam haec est etiam quaedam species vocis dilecti, vocis adjurantis et quasi juridicialis: Primum quaerite regnum Dei et justitiam ejus et haec omnia adjicientur vobis (Matth. VI), ut hoc aequum esse debeat ipso dilecto dictante, quatenus Deo adhaerentibus necessarius creaturae consequenter deserviat usus. Docuit plane et confirmavit proprio ipse dilectus testimonio, quando hujus mei comparem 1107Cstudii, talem extulit praeconio, Maria, inquiens, optimam partem elegit, quae non auferetur ab ea (Luc. X). Nempe et haec vox dilecti, ut merito hoc meae dormitionis studium praeponere debeam omnium vigiliis negotiorum. Sed quid est, quod ex hac voce dilecti mei, hoc est ex sancta Scriptura audivi et didici, quando per mentis quietem in ejus contemplatione dormivi? Istud nimirum quod vobis nunc, o filiae Jerusalem, de ipsius dilecti mei virtute narrabo. Ecce iste venit saliens in 100 montibus transiliens colles. Ecce, inquit, iste venit. Venire ejus dicitur non secundum divinitatem sed secundum humanitatem. Ille enim qui secundum divinitatem incirconscriptus et illocalis 1107Dest, quomodo venire diceretur, qui immobilis et incommutabilis existens, sicut semper in se ipso unus idemque permanet, ut nec loco mutetur, nec aliqua varietate in diversa feratur. Sed quoties in corda sanctorum venire dicetur, hoc non secundum sui aliquam motabilitatem, sed secundum illorum aptitudinem, qua se minus aut majus ejus amori applicant, per inspirationem suam venire afferetur. Secundum humanitatem ergo venit, cum passibilis propter nos factus pati voluit humanae consuetudinis localem translationem: nam ut visibilis fieret de coelo venit et humanam naturam assumpsit, in qua passus et mortuus resurrexit; et in coelum ascendit, quod totum fecit moveri, et quasi de uno ad aliud venire. Hoc itaque modo veniendi 1108Avenit dilectus, saliens in montibus, quando in tempore dispensationis multis et magnificis emicuit saltibus in sublimium virtutum montibus.

Montes enim quidam sunt praecipuae et eminentes virtutes in quibus dilectus iste saltus fecit, quando de virtute in virtutem quosdam progressus fecit: Excelsus enim super coelos Deus ad terram humilis nascendo venit, de quo humilitatis monte in alium montem obedientiae ascendit, factus est enim obediens Deo Patri usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis (Philip. II); quam suscipiendo in montem patientiae saltum fecit; de quo postremo in montem gloriae conscendit, ubi victoriosae mortis triumphum resurgendo et in coelum ascendendo collocavit.

1108BIste ergo dilectus venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles; quia quidquid sapientiae et intellectus, quidquid consilii et fortitudinis, quidquid scientiae et pietatis, quidquid divini timoris, quidquid denique alicujus honestatis, justitiae et sanctitatis esse unquam potuit vel potest, in isto dilecto veluti in capite prae omnibus ejus membris, hoc est sanctis, qui colles dicuntur, sublimius et praeclarius effulsit. Hoc ex parte in libris Evangeliorum aspicere quilibet intelligens potest, qualiter iste dilectus salierit in montibus, hoc est in virtutibus verbo et exemplo, transiliens omnium sanctorum exempla et documenta suo singulari et incomparabili operationis et doctrinae praedicamento; exsultavit 1108Cut gigas ad currendam viam quia a summo coelo egressio ejus et occursus ejus usque ad summum ejus (Psal. XVIII).

101 VERS. 9.-- Similis est dilectus meus capreae, hinnuloque cervorum: en iste stat post parietem nostrum respiciens per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos.

Unde similis dicitur capreae hinnuloque cervorum: capreae enim naturale est semper ascensus quaerere, et cum sanctis gratiarum distributio diverso tribuatur modo: Alii quidem sic, alii vero sic, sol unigenito non ad mensuram dat Deus spiritum, quia in ipso habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter (I Cor. VII; Joan. III; Coloss. II). Sancti enim 1108Din virtutum studio nunc ascendunt, nunc non ascendunt quia in eorum meritis gratia illa quam habent nunc operatur nunc quiescit, quatenus hoc eis sit ad humilitatis custodiam quod non semper in promptu habent collatae virtutis gratiam. Isti autem dilecto non ad tempus, neque per intervalla, sed sine intermissione virtutum constat gratia, sicut de eo scriptum est, quia descendit Spiritus sanctus in columbae specie et mansit super eum (Luc. III; Joan. I).

Hinnulo quoque cervorum assimilatur propter velocitatem, quia sicut hinnulus propter juvenilis corporis levitatem multo velocior cervo est; sic dilectus iste quasi hinnulus cervorum, hoc est filius patriarcharum de quorum stirpe processit, longe 1109Apraestantior et agilior virtutum efficacia et verborum sapientia et ipsorum antiquorum Patrum studiis et documentis.

Cum ergo omnes iste dilectus exhortando et praesiliendo ad virtutum studia provocet, quidam autem pro posse suo sequantur, quidam fragilitate obstante sequi se posse desperent, nonnulli peccatorum mole depressi ad ea resurgere diffidant, aufert eis omnem occasionem diffidendi dilectae praetendens dilecti hujus pietatem ineffabilem omnes ad sui gratiam misericorditer invitantem et subdit: En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, etc. Unus est paries generalis, peccati scilicet originalis; sed iste paries in multos diffunditur parietes 1109Bspeciales actualis peccati. Ex originali namque peccato quasi ex quadam massa processerunt multa et diversa actualia peccata, quia postquam per originale peccatum primi parentis lapsi sunt, genus infirmitatis hujus in posteros transfunditur, videlicet ad peccata semper esse proclives. Verum iste generalis paries destrui coepit veniente per carnem Dei filio, cujus sanguine tandem submotus et dissipatus est, quando solvens inimicitias inter Deum et hominem reconciliavit nos Deo (Eph. II); et ne possit reformari, quotidie destruitur in Ecclesia per gratiam baptismi.

Specialis vero paries in diversis diverso constituitur modo, quia in alio est vitium superbiae, in 1109Calio avaritiae, 102 in isto luxuriae, in illo impudicitiae, in aliquo obedientiae, in nonnullo impatientiae, sive aliud quodcunque vitium, quod juxta ipsius vitii qualitatem, et modum et numerum, facit qualemcunque parietem inter hominem et Deum quoque vitium majus vel crebrius sive numerosius et in homine, eo gravius et immobilius pondus est in pariete.

Sed post istum parietem sive generalem peccati originalis, sive specialem actualis stat dilectus iste, quia paratus est misericorditer suscipere, quicunque aliquo tali remoto pariete, in eodem destruendo per poenitentiam ei studuerint repropinquare. Stare quippe est adjuvantis, sedere judicantis. Post parietem stat, quia dum ad nos per gratiam suam disponit 1109Dvenire, obstante pariete peccati, quasi compellitur stare. Primo namque diu stetit ne veniret ad amovendum illum parietem peccati originalis, propter multa prohibendo adventum ejus, multis afflictionibus et adversitatibus quibus insequebatur eos qui adventum ejus desiderabant et exspectabant, quo veniente sciebant hunc parietem destruendum per sanguinem ipsius et Deo se reconciliandos.

Stetit ergo hac de causa et venire distulit respiciens interim per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos. Quid enim erant fenestrae in pariete nisi prophetae aliique doctores legis divinae quorum doctrina et praedicatione quasi quosdam exitus respiciendi Deus inveniret per quos aliquod gratiae 1110Asuae lumen profunderet quo illuminatum et admonitum genus humanum, desisteret retardare hujus dilecti adventum saluti suae profuturum, tantae malitiae quasi cujusdam parietis interpositione

Cancelli vero, id est anterior pars aedificii, fuerunt praecedentes antiqui patres, videlicet patriarchae ante legem Christum annuntiantes, per quos longe post venturus ex parte prospiciebat signis et portentis et quibusdam rationum documentis; admonendo ne impedirent pariete malorum suorum futura tantae salutis suae tempora.

Tamdiu ergo stetit post parietem nostrum misericorditer prospiciendo et verbo, lege, signis, atque prodigiis consulendo, donec tandem per motus 1110Bafflictione suorum crebro clamantium: Veni, Domine, et noli tardare, relaxa facinora plebis tuae, compressis omnium terrarum motibus sub Caesare Augusto, et firmissima verissimaque pace Dei ordinatione disposita, quasi concusso jam pariete obstantis malitiae coepit desideratam diu faciem dilectus 103 iste nascendo ostendere, atque deinceps praedicando, moriendo, resurgendo, in coelum ascendendo, sicque per totum orbem Evangelii sui legem spargendo, diu oppositum quotidie per gratiam baptismi destruere peccati originalis parietem.

Porro fenestrae et cancelli in pariete actualis peccati, per quas quotidie prospicitur dilectus iste, 1110Csunt Evangeliorum et apostolorum, caeterorumque sanctorum patrum exempla et documenta; ibi quidem fenestrae ubi scientiae et intelligentiae lumen cordibus nostris infundunt, ut videre possimus qualiter cujusque peccati parietem inter nos et Deum positum amoveamus; cancelli vero eo loco ubi ex eorum scriptis Deum ad nos respicientem per contemplationis virtutem ex parte cognoscimus et ex parte prophetamus (I Cor. XIII), ut dum futurae vitae gloriam vel poenam attendimus, peccati parietem a Deo nos separantem, quotidie destruere laboremus.

Amplius. Veniens in carne Dei Filius, stetit post parietem mortalitatis nostrae, prospiciens ad nos per fenestras et cancellos divinitatis suae; qui 1110Detiam Deus claruit ex miraculorum potentia et tamen latuit ex humanae passibilitatis natura. Qui enim per fenestras et cancellos prospicit, nec totus videtur, nec totus non videtur: sic nimirum et redemptor noster in carne veniens Deum se ex miraculis ostendit, ex passionibus vero occultavit. Post parietem ergo humanae passibilitatis stetit, quia ex humanitate occultus inter homines, non ut Deus venit; per fenestras vero et cancellos prospexit, quia miseratione divina toti generi humano perennia salutis dona dictavit. Et quia dilectam quam intus misericordiae suae intuitu attraxit, foris quoque praedicationis verbo instruxerit eamdem, subdendo manifestat:

VERS. 10-- En dilectus meus loquitur mihi: Surge, propera, amica mea, columba mea, formo sa mea, et veni. 1111A

Locutio ista dilecti tripliciter distinguitur pulchritudine appellationis, adhortationis et causae: appellationis quidem, dum dicit: amica mea, columba mea, formosa mea, adhortationis vero dum dicit: Surge, propera, veni; causae dum dicit: Jam enim hiems transiit, imber abiit et recessit, flores apparuerunt, tempus putationis advenit.
